subject: WharfEdge: New region sizing + fallback lanes proposal
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@wharfedge.ai>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@wharfedge.ai
Date: 2026-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask - APAC microregion + EU compliant pool

Jordan — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Product team is excited about the latency improvements. We have two asks up front so procurement can draft the PO: a small APAC microregion (Singapore) to meet <=60ms P95 for our customer-facing inference, and an EU-compliant pool (Frankfurt) with SOC2-ready audit logs.

High level numbers from our side: ~350k tokens/day seeded, peak 8 qps sustained for 3 hours. We expect growth 40% q/q after launch. Can you provide a proposal for sizing + an operational fallback (if APAC capacity is constrained, route to eu-read replicas with kv-cache warmers)?

+Anna
Anna Li
Head of Platform
WharfEdge

Thanks Anna — looping in Irene (infra/ops) and Karthik (regional capacity planning). Quick reply with next steps:

- Irene will draft a sizing baseline and fallback lanes based on your QPS/token profile.
- Karthik will map expected reserved-node tranches and lead time for Singapore and Frankfurt.
- Jordan (me) will coordinate contract / SOW language with Marissa.

Irene/Karthik — can you run two scenarios (conservative: 8 qps sustained, 40% growth q/q) and (aggressive: 12 qps sustained, 60% growth) and include burst backstop options (US or EU) plus expected unit-cost delta for cross-region routing?

Best,
Jordan

redwood.com

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Li <anna@wharfedge.ai>
Date: 2026-06-07T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask - APAC microregion + EU compliant pool

On Mon, Jun 7, 2026 at 11:03 AM jordan_blake@redwood.com wrote:
> Irene/Karthik — can you run two scenarios...

Attached a short baseline in the Drive link (also copied below). Summary:

- Conservative: 1 x small dedicated pool (2x A10G-style nodes equivalent) + 1 standby node in EU for immediate failover. Estimated steady tokens/month: ~10M, cost uplift ~28% vs hosted.
- Aggressive: 2 x small dedicated pools (hot/hot in APAC + EU) with cross-region warmers, expected steady tokens/month ~16M, cost uplift ~45%.

Operational notes:
- KV-cache warmers reduce cold-start latency but require prefix population. We recommend a brief pre-warming window at predicted ramp times (we can automate via our rollout hooks).
- Fallback routing: prefer EU read-replica lane with TTL-based consistency for <2s divergence on user sessions. For hard outages, route to US compute pool and return to APAC gracefully.

I'll produce a short Sizing & Fallback appendix for Marissa to fold into the SOW.

-Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Ops
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna@wharfedge.ai>
Date: 2026-06-08T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask - APAC microregion + EU compliant pool

Quick numbers from capacity planning (rounded):

- Conservative scenario (8 qps sustained): APAC pool = 2 nodes (reserved), EU pool = 1 standby node; expected commit: 12-month reserved term. Lead time: 6–8 weeks to secure additional allocation if we don't have immediate spare capacity.
- Aggressive (12 qps): APAC = 3 nodes, EU = 2 nodes; lead time: 8–12 weeks. Recommend a tranche-based commit (start with conservative + 12-week review to add tranche).

Cost sensitivity: cross-region failover to US increases egress and infra delta (+~15–22% per-token effective cost during failover). We'll show the exact per-token delta in the appendix.

Action ask for Jordan/Marissa: confirm which initial tranche WharfEdge prefers (conservative vs aggressive) and whether they need SOC2 evidence pre-signature or can accept a conditional clause in the SOW.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@wharfedge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask - APAC microregion + EU compliant pool

Anna — thanks for the prompt details. Short summary + next steps so procurement has a clear path: 

1) Recommendation (start): Conservative tranche — 2-node APAC reserved pool + 1-node EU standby. This hits your latency targets at launch and keeps lead time short.
2) Optional (growth): Auto-tranche clause at +40% MAU triggers to add an extra APAC node (12-week notice).
3) SOC2/compliance: Marissa will attach SOC2 report and audit evidence. If you need the SOC2 attestation before PO, let us know and we’ll expedite.
4) SOW: Marissa — can you attach the Sizing & Fallback appendix and SOW template (see attached) and return a redline by EOD Friday?

If that all sounds good, I'll route a draft SOW + pricing and we can get procurement to sign.

Cheers,
Jordan
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
